title: Pediatric RSI — Decision & Dosing Card

changelog.change: Initial entry — the 7-step sequence adapted for children, induction/paralytic selection by scenario, weight-based dose ranges, and the peds-specific pitfalls.

purpose: Decision support for choosing induction and paralytic agents in a child needing emergency intubation, plus the weight-based doses and the paediatric-specific hazards. Exact per-drug doses are on the linked drug cards.

items: Preparation — weight (measured or estimated), SOAP-ME, size the tube/blade/LMA from the weight zone, draw up push-dose adrenaline, set the ventilator.
Preoxygenation — 3–5 min of high-FiO2; apnoeic oxygenation with nasal cannula (kids desaturate fast — low FRC, high O2 consumption).

Pretreatment — atropine 0.02 mg/kg (no minimum dose in current PALS) if age < 1 y, or if using succinylcholine, or for pre-existing bradycardia. Fentanyl 1–2 mcg/kg over 60 s if a sympathetic surge is undesirable (head injury, cardiac lesion).
Paralysis with induction — give the induction agent then the paralytic in rapid succession.
Positioning — shoulder roll in infants (large occiput); ear-to-sternal-notch in older children.
Placement with proof — waveform capnography + bilateral lung sliding/breath sounds; note the depth.
Post-intubation — analgesia and sedation infusion, lung-protective settings, NG/OG tube, confirm with CXR.

rows: 1–2 mg/kg IV (bronchodilator, preserves drive; fine in raised ICP)
0.5–1 mg/kg IV (reduced) — or etomidate 0.2–0.3 mg/kg (single dose; adrenal-suppression concern in sepsis)
both acceptable; avoid hypotension above all
Preferred default. Onset ~ 45–60 s; duration 30–45 min. Reversible with sugammadex 16 mg/kg
1.5–2 mg/kg IV (2–3 mg/kg in infants) + atropine
Faster offset but AVOID with: hyperkalaemia risk, burns/crush > 48–72 h, denervation, myopathy (risk of hyperkalaemic arrest and MH). Give atropine first in all children

body.text: Paediatric pitfalls: children desaturate within seconds — preoxygenate hard and keep nasal O2 running. The large occiput causes neck flexion — use a shoulder roll under 2 y. Uncuffed tube leak too large → step up a half size or switch to cuffed. Bradycardia during laryngoscopy is hypoxia until proven otherwise — stop, bag, reassess. Have a weight-appropriate LMA and a front-of-neck plan ready before you start.

buildNote: Dose ranges shown for decision support; the drug cards compute exact volumes from the entered weight.
